newsitem.title: KENYA: SOCCER-KENYA HOLD NIGERIA 1-1 IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KENYA HOLD NIGERIA 1-1 IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Nigeria's Super Eagles were held to a surprise 1-1 draw by Kenya in their World Cup Africa Group One qualifying match in Nairobi on Sunday.
The Kenyans took the lead in the 25th minute through Ken Simiyu who beat Nigerian goalkeeper Joseph Dosu with a header from close range after a corner by Eric Ochieng.
Jonathan Akpoborie struck the equaliser for the Olympic champions in the 48th minute, heading in a corner from Finidi George.
A capacity 60,000-strong crowd, including Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi and members of his cabinet, packed the Moi International Sports Centre in Nairobi for the match.

Nigerian coach Shuaibu Amodu criticised the state of the pitch, but Kenya's German coach Reinhardt Fabisch, who sacked the existing team and replaced it two months ago with a youthful outfit whose age average is just 21, was well satisfied.
"This is a very young team and they have done their job very well," said Fabisch. "We've played one of the best teams in the world and I am extremely impressed and proud of them."

Nigeria's team, all Europe-based professionals, made no serious attempts at the Kenyan goal in the first half but were close several times in the second, with substitute Tijani Babangida and Augustine Okocha key in Nigerian raids.

Nigeria - Joseph Dosu, Chidi Nwanu, Celestine Babayoro, Sunday Oliseh, Uche Ukechukwu, Taribo West, Finidi George (Tijani Babangida), Daniel Amokachi, Jonathan Akpoborie (Victor Ikpeba), Augustine Okocha, Garba Lawal.
Kenya - Francis Onyiso, Musa Otieno, John Lichuku, Josiah Ougo, John Odhiambo, Eric Ochieng, Maurice Wambua (Seif Mutie), Mohamed Sharrif (Tielen Oguta), Tom Ogweno, Ken Simiyu.
